analysis.title: Monthly Hedge Fund Performance Update, October 2026
key_insights: Hedge funds were down 1.3% in October (strategy-weighted) as crowded AI positions weakened, momentum reversed and managers cut risk. The equal-weighted average was -1.5%, and the YTD strategy-weighted figure is 5.1%.
Multi-PM managers had their worst month on GS records, worse than March 2020. Losses came from both fundamental and systematic L/S strategies. Multi-PM returned -2.3% in October and 0.1% YTD.

Global fundamental L/S alpha, excluding beta, was -1.75%. That is the worst monthly alpha since July and second worst in more than four years. Long-side losses drove it, with short-side losses a smaller part.
Equity fundamental L/S returned -2.1% in October and 5.8% YTD. TMT was the steepest loser at -4.8% for the month (12.2% YTD), as investors rotated out of the AI ecosystem. Healthcare lost only 0.2%.
Systematic macro / CTA was the only strategy positive in October at +0.9%. It leads all strategies YTD at 14.9%, and its one-year return is 17.2%.

The S&P 500 fell less than 1% in October with most constituents advancing, which masked a sharp unwind in crowded AI and momentum exposures. Doubts about returns on large AI capex hit semiconductors, other AI proxies and hyperscalers, while SMID caps benefited from the rotation.
Credit (-1.6%), discretionary macro (-0.4%) and relative value (-1.3%) faced mixed conditions amid sharp moves in rates, currencies and commodities. Event driven returned -0.8% and quant -0.6%.
By region, Asia managers lost the most at -3.5% because China exposure hurt. Americas returned -1.5% and Europe -0.4%.

Fundamental equity L/S dispersion is wide. The October median was -1.9%, with a 10th percentile of -8.7% and a 90th of 4.3%. Dispersion (75th minus 25th percentile) was 6.0% for October and 14.7% YTD.
Long-biased equity L/S funds lost 2.7% in October versus -2.0% for variable net and -1.7% for market neutral/low net. Generalists and sector specialists both returned -2.1%.
Allocator-type returns were similar in October, between -1.2% (pensions) and -1.6% (endowments and foundations).

sector_views.rationale: Fundamental L/S TMT funds lost 4.8% in October as investors rotated out of AI-ecosystem names, though TMT is still up 12.2% YTD. This is a description of hedge fund performance, not a formal sector call.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The index looked calm, but a sharp rotation and an unwind in crowded AI and momentum positions sat underneath it.
Nasdaq underperformed the broader market as AI and semiconductor stocks sold off.
Small and mid caps benefited from the rotation out of AI-linked large caps.
Escalating Middle East tensions drove Brent higher in October. The report gives no price level.

risk_factors: Doubts about returns on AI capital expenditure could extend the drawdown in semiconductors, AI proxies and hyperscalers.
Crowded momentum and AI positioning can unwind quickly while the index looks calm.
Middle East escalation is lifting oil.
China equity exposure is a source of losses for Asia-focused managers.
vol_and_positioning: Crowded AI and momentum positions unwound sharply in October, and managers cut risk.
Multi-PM managers had the worst month on GS records, surpassing March 2020.
Factor volatility and single-stock dispersion were high beneath muted index-level moves.
Systematic macro / CTA was the only positive strategy in October.
geopolitical: Escalating Middle East tensions drove a sharp increase in Brent crude in October.
China exposure hurt Asia-based hedge fund managers in October.
